# TradingLab

> Crypto trading strategy backtester with exhaustive parameter optimization. Test SMA crossover strategies against historical OHLC data with configurable leverage and ATR-based trailing stops. Free, open-source, runs entirely in the browser.

TradingLab is a single-page web application available at https://tradinglab.vip. It is built with Next.js 16 and React 19, and all computation runs client-side in a Web Worker so the UI stays responsive during optimization.

---

## Overview

TradingLab lets you upload historical crypto price data (OHLC CSV) and exhaustively test all combinations of SMA crossover strategy parameters to find the best-performing configuration. It compares results against a buy-and-hold baseline and provides a day-by-day trade log for the top strategy.

**Author:** Wesley Coetzee (https://wezzcoetzee.com)  
**License:** Open source (https://github.com/wezzcoetzee/tradinglab)  
**Live site:** https://tradinglab.vip

---

## CSV Data Format

Your input CSV file must contain the following columns (order does not matter, headers are required):

| Column | Type   | Description                        |
|--------|--------|------------------------------------|
| high   | number | Period high price                  |
| low    | number | Period low price                   |
| close  | number | Period close price                 |
| date   | string | Human-readable date (DD/MM/YYYY)   |

- Minimum required rows: 160 (warmup period for SMA/ATR pre-computation)
- The CSV validator strips invalid rows and reports errors before optimization begins
- Sample data files for BTC, ETH, and SOL are bundled at `/BTC.csv`, `/ETH.csv`, `/SOL.csv`

---

## Strategy Configuration

The following parameters are configurable before running optimization:

### Starting Capital
- Default: $1,000
- The initial portfolio value used for all backtests in the optimization run

### Trading Fee
- Default: 0.05%
- Fee percentage applied per trade (per position open/close/transition)
- Example: 0.05 means 0.05% fee per trade

### SMA Range
- Min SMA period: default 2, minimum allowed 2
- Max SMA period: default 200, maximum tested is 200
- The optimizer tests all integer SMA periods within this range

### ATR Trailing Stop (optional toggle)
- Default: disabled
- When enabled, the optimizer additionally tests ATR-based trailing stop configurations alongside each SMA/leverage combination
- Enabling ATR significantly increases the number of configurations tested

---

## Optimization Parameters

The backtester performs exhaustive search across all parameter combinations:

### Leverage Levels
Both long leverage and short leverage are independently varied across:
- 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 1.75×, 2×, 2.25×, 2.5×, 2.75×, 3×

Long and short leverage are tested independently, meaning each SMA period is paired with every combination of (longLeverage × shortLeverage).

### ATR Configurations (when ATR enabled)
60 ATR configurations are tested per SMA/leverage combination:
- **ATR Periods:** 10, 14, 20
- **ATR Multipliers:** 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4
- **Partial Close Percentages:** 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%

Total ATR configs = 3 periods × 5 multipliers × 4 close percentages = 60

### Total Configurations
- Without ATR: `(smaMax - smaMin + 1) × 9 (long leverages) × 9 (short leverages)`
- With ATR: multiply the above by 60 ATR configurations

---

## Strategy Logic

TradingLab implements a **SMA crossover strategy** with optional ATR trailing stops.

### Signal Generation
- **Long signal:** price > SMA — open or maintain a long position
- **Short signal:** price < SMA — open or maintain a short position
- Signals are evaluated once per day (candle close)

### Position Actions
Each day one of the following actions is taken:

| Action                      | Description                                                   |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| OPEN_LONG                   | No position → enter long at current price                     |
| OPEN_SHORT                  | No position → enter short at current price                    |
| CLOSE_LONG                  | Price dropped below SMA → exit long position                  |
| CLOSE_SHORT                 | Price rose above SMA → exit short position                    |
| TRANSITION_LONG_TO_SHORT    | Direct flip from long to short (fee applied once)             |
| TRANSITION_SHORT_TO_LONG    | Direct flip from short to long (fee applied once)             |
| HOLD                        | Signal unchanged, no action taken                             |
| ATR_PARTIAL_CLOSE           | ATR trailing stop triggered — partial close executed          |

### Leverage and PnL
- Leveraged PnL = (price change % × leverage) × position value
- Liquidation occurs if leveraged loss exceeds 100% of position collateral
- On liquidation, the position is closed at zero value

### ATR Trailing Stop Logic
When ATR is enabled:
1. An extreme price is tracked from position entry (highest price for longs, lowest for shorts)
2. The stop triggers when price moves `ATR × multiplier` against the position from the extreme
3. On trigger: `closePercent`% of the position is closed (10%, 25%, 50%, or 100%)
4. Closed capital moves to "sideline" (uninvested cash earning no return)
5. The remaining open portion continues until the next SMA signal

### Fee Calculation
- Fee is charged on the notional value of each trade (entry value × leverage)
- Transitions (long→short or short→long) are treated as a single trade for fee purposes
- ATR partial closes incur fees on the partial close amount

---

## Backtest Engine Internals

### SMA Pre-computation
- SMA values for all periods in the configured range are pre-computed once before optimization
- Pre-computation uses a rolling sum for efficiency: O(n × periods) total

### ATR Pre-computation
- ATR (Average True Range) is pre-computed for periods 10, 14, and 20
- True Range = max(high−low, |high−prevClose|, |low−prevClose|)
- ATR uses a Wilder smoothing (exponential) average

### Web Worker Execution
- The optimization loop runs in a browser Web Worker to avoid blocking the main thread
- Progress updates are sent to the main thread every 100 configurations
- The optimization can be cancelled mid-run

### Result Tracking
- Without ATR: all results are collected and sorted by total return
- With ATR: a top-K min-heap is used to track only the top 1,000 results by total return, reducing memory usage

---

## Result Metrics

Each backtest result includes:

| Metric           | Description                                                    |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| totalReturn      | Percentage gain/loss vs starting capital                       |
| finalBalance     | Final portfolio value (collateral in open position)            |
| finalCollateral  | Value of collateral held in the final position                 |
| totalFees        | Total fees paid across all trades                              |
| totalTrades      | Number of position opens/closes/transitions                    |
| atrTriggerCount  | Number of times ATR trailing stop fired (if ATR enabled)       |
| isLiquidated     | Whether the position was liquidated at any point               |
| liquidationDay   | Day index of liquidation (if applicable)                       |
| liquidationDate  | Date string of liquidation (if applicable)                     |

### Day-by-Day Log
For the best-performing strategy, a full day-by-day log is available with:
- Date, price, SMA value
- Action taken that day
- Current position (type, entry price, leverage)
- Balance, PnL, fees for that day
- Portfolio value (balance + open position value)

---

## Buy & Hold Baseline

The optimizer also calculates a simple buy-and-hold baseline for comparison:
- Purchases the asset on the first day of the dataset
- Holds until the last day
- Reports purchase price, final price, and percentage gain
- Compared against the best SMA strategy result

---

## Results Views

### Results Table
- Lists top strategies sorted by total return (descending)
- Shows SMA period, long leverage, short leverage, ATR config (if any), total return, fees, trades
- Paginated (configurable rows per page)

### SMA Comparison Table
- Groups results by SMA period
- Shows best return per SMA period with associated leverage and ATR config
- Useful for identifying which SMA periods perform best regardless of leverage

### Day-by-Day Table
- Detailed trade log for the single best-performing configuration
- Shows every day with price, SMA, action, balance, PnL, and portfolio value

## Default Configuration Values

| Parameter      | Default | Min  | Max  |
|----------------|---------|------|------|
| startingCapital| $1,000  | >0   | —    |
| tradingFee     | 0.05%   | 0    | 100  |
| smaMin         | 2       | 2    | 50   |
| smaMax         | 200     | 3    | 200  |
| atrEnabled     | false   | —    | —    |

---

## Usage Guide

### Step 1: Prepare CSV Data
Ensure your CSV has the required columns: `high`, `low`, `close`, `date` (DD/MM/YYYY format). Minimum 160 rows of data required.

Sample files are provided: download BTC.csv, ETH.csv, or SOL.csv from the site to use as a template.

### Step 2: Upload and Validate
Click "Upload CSV" on the backtester page and select your file. The app validates the file and displays the row count and any errors.

### Step 3: Configure Strategy
Set your parameters:
- Starting Capital (default $1,000)
- Trading Fee % (default 0.05%)
- SMA Min/Max range (default 2–200)
- Enable ATR Trailing Stop if desired

### Step 4: Run Optimization
Click "Run Optimization". The Web Worker begins testing all parameter combinations. A progress bar shows completion percentage. You can cancel at any time.

### Step 5: Analyze Results
Once complete:
- Review the Results Table for top-performing strategies
- Use the SMA Comparison Table to see performance by SMA period
- Open the Day-by-Day Table for the best strategy's full trade history
- Compare against the Buy & Hold baseline shown in the metrics cards

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Does TradingLab require an account or API key?**  
A: No. Everything runs in your browser. No data is sent to any server (except for Google Analytics page views).

**Q: How long does optimization take?**  
A: Depends on dataset size and SMA range. A full run (SMA 2–200, no ATR) on a 3-year daily dataset typically completes in a few seconds. Enabling ATR multiplies the computation by ~60x.

**Q: Can I use minute/hourly data?**  
A: Yes, as long as each row has `high`, `low`, `close`, and `date` columns. The strategy logic is timeframe-agnostic.

**Q: What does "sideline" mean in the day-by-day log?**  
A: When an ATR trailing stop partially closes a position, the closed capital moves to "sideline" — it is not reinvested until the next SMA signal triggers a new position.

**Q: Why is there a 160-row minimum?**  
A: The warmup period of 160 candles is needed to pre-compute SMA values up to period 160 and to initialize ATR calculations. Rows used for warmup are not included in backtesting.

**Q: Are short positions supported?**  
A: Yes. The strategy goes short (with configurable leverage) when price is below the SMA. Long and short leverage can be set independently.
